_comment: CAMPAIGN midfield income platforms (single-player only – multiplayer instead runs the single central boss-spawning platform). Three neutral rigs stand in the open water between the two bases. When only ONE side's mobile ships are in a rig's capture lane, it is slowly seized for that side; MORE ships nearby seize it faster. A rig must be dragged back through neutral before the other side can flip it. HOME-FIELD advantage means you hold the rig on YOUR half easily even when out-numbered, so the CENTRE rig is the real prize. Neither side snowballs: extra rigs give diminishing income and a side that's behind captures faster. Edit freely.

_field_notes.enabled_from_level: 1-based campaign level the rigs first appear on (level 5 = the 5th level in the select grid).
_field_notes.count: How many rigs to field. Positions come from `positions` when its length matches, else the rigs are spread evenly across the midfield.
_field_notes.positions: Each rig's spot as a fraction (0..1) of the open water between the forts (0 = just off the player fort, 1 = just off the enemy fort). A rig in your half is a HOME rig; one near 0.5 is neutral ground.
_field_notes.income_per_rig: Gold/sec for a side's FIRST held rig. Further rigs are worth `holdings_falloff`x the previous one.
_field_notes.capture_seconds: Seconds for a SINGLE ship to seize a fully-neutral rig (or to drag it from one owner back to neutral).
_field_notes.capture_radius: How close (world px, measured along the battle line) a ship must be to count toward a rig's capture.
_field_notes.ship_speedup: Each extra ship beyond the first adds this fraction to the capture speed.
_field_notes.max_ship_speedup: Cap on the ship-count speed multiplier, so a swarm can't seize instantly.
_field_notes.decay_seconds: If > 0, a rig with NO ships nearby slowly bleeds back toward neutral over this many seconds. 0 = captures are permanent until contested.
_field_notes.home_advantage: A side seizes/holds a rig on its OWN half this many times faster; the invader gets the reciprocal. Lets you keep your own rig when out-numbered and makes the centre rig the battleground. 1.0 disables it.
_field_notes.holdings_falloff: ANTI-SNOWBALL. Each additional rig a side holds is worth this fraction of the previous for INCOME. <1 makes hoarding give little marginal value; 1.0 = linear.
_field_notes.comeback_per_rig: ANTI-SNOWBALL. You capture this much faster per rig you hold FEWER than the opponent, so a team that lost the midfield can fight a rig back.
_field_notes.max_comeback: Cap on the comeback capture-speed multiplier.
